newsitem.title: GERMANY: German roasters still shun coffee market.
newsitem.headline: German roasters still shun coffee market.

text.p: German green coffee buyers were shocked by renewed futures surges after the rallies seen in recent weeks, a spokesman for the German coffee industry association DKV said on Wednesday.
But raw materials buyers said buying at above 200 cents/lb was out of the question.
New York May arabicas soared to their highest levels since mid-1994.
"This is amazing...the pressure is rising enormously, but I would warn against panic reactions," the spokesman said.
Unlike their European competitors, German roasters have to pay a 2.15 marks tax on roasted coffee sales per 0.5 kilos.
The average retail price has not changed much from early January levels of 6.80 marks.
He also said a second round of price rises may be necessary after roasters have implemented currently planned increases by 1.50 marks per 0.5 kilos effective March 10.
"There is a need for further increases if prices stay where they are but it is too early to say anyting concrete," he said.
He added it was unlikely roasters would seek to replace expensive coffees in their blends with less costly material.
"Roasters will not change the quality of their coffee because they know it is crucial to their success," he said.
This echoed a remark made by the chairman of family-owned J.J. Darboven, Albert Darboven, on Tuesday.
"...we'd rather sell less coffee than compromise on quality," Darboven said.
